t: You're looking at the site of the Hanover Gallery, which opened in June 1948 at 32A St. George's Street and closed on the thirty-first of March 1973. It took its name from nearby Hanover Square. It was an important centre for modern art. It was founded by the German art expert Erica Brausen, together with the financier and collector Arthur Jeffress. Brausen was an art dealer who championed several influential contemporary artists early on, most notably Francis Bacon. So this is a place where some of that modern work first found its audience.
